description: Elemental Creepers 1.4 ported to Better than Adventure! (BTA) 8.0.1 on Babric. Nine creepers that flood, freeze, burn, electrify, bury, launch and haunt. Ships none of the original's art - the mod reads it from your own copy at runtime.

releases.notes:
All nine creepers are now in the guidebook.

## The creepers are in the guidebook

Open the guidebook and the Creatures section runs on past BTA's own mobs into
the water, fire, ice, electric, earth, psychic, cookie, magma and ghost
creepers, each with its picture, its health, what it drops and a line about
what it does to the ground when it goes off.

Nothing was broken before — the pages had simply never been asked for. Adding a
mob to the game and adding it to the book are two separate things, and only the
first had ever been done. The descriptions have been in this mod's language
file since the port was written, waiting for a page to be printed on.

The figures on each page are read off a live creeper rather than typed out by
hand, so if BTA ever changes what a creeper is worth, the pages follow it
instead of quietly going stale.

Nothing about how the creepers behave has changed. This is the book only.

## Install

Drop `elementalcreepers-1.4.3+8.0.1.jar` into `mods/`. Drop-in replacement for
1.4.2.

releases.notes:
Preventive: this mod could, in principle, have stopped other mods from
finishing their startup. It was not observed doing so, but a sibling port was,
and the exposure here is the same shape.

## Nothing escapes startup any more

BTA gives every mod a chance to finish setting itself up once the game is
built, and all of those run from a single shared list. If any one of them
fails, the rest of the list is abandoned — every mod after the failing one
simply never runs its own setup, and nothing anywhere says so. What you see
instead is an unexplained crash in some third mod later on.

This mod adds its creepers to every biome's monster list in that step. It
already left deliberately-empty lists alone, which happens to sidestep the
common case, but a biome that hands out a non-empty locked list would still
have thrown. Now such a biome is skipped and counted in the log, and the whole
startup step is wrapped so nothing can escape it regardless.

You lose creepers in a biome that refuses them. Nothing else changes.

## Install

Drop `elementalcreepers-1.4.2+8.0.1.jar` into `mods/`. Drop-in replacement for
1.4.1.

releases.notes:
One fix: an asset pack built on someone else's machine is now switched on
instead of being ignored.

## Packs built elsewhere now get used

The mod reads the original's art out of a copy you supply and writes it as a
texture pack. That pack is just a folder, so people copy finished ones to each
other — and if you got yours that way, it did nothing. The eight skinned
creepers wore the plain vanilla creeper texture, exactly as if no pack were
there at all.

The pack was only ever switched on along the two paths that require a copy of
`ElementalCreepers_v1.4.zip` on your own disk: the one where the mod had just
built the pack, and the one where it checked that the archive it was built from
was still where it left it. A machine that never had the archive fails that
check by definition, so the mod concluded there was nothing to do and returned
without ever looking in the texture pack folder. Nothing else in the game
switches a pack on for you, so it stayed off.

It is now switched on whenever a pack is present, whether or not this copy of
the game could have built it. You need the original only to *make* a pack, not
to use one.

The startup log now distinguishes "no art anywhere" from "a pack built
elsewhere, used as it stands".

## Install

Drop `elementalcreepers-1.4.1+8.0.1.jar` into `mods/`. Nothing else changes;
this is a drop-in replacement for 1.4.0.

releases.notes:
Elemental Creepers 1.4 for Minecraft b1.7.3, ported to **Better than Adventure 8.0.1**.

Nine creepers that do something other than blow a hole in the ground: water floods, ice freezes
water to ice and lava to obsidian, fire and magma burn, electric calls down lightning, earth buries,
psychic throws you into the sky, cookie is harmless, and the ghost creeper comes back after one of
the others dies.

Works in singleplayer and on a dedicated server.

## Install

Drop `elementalcreepers-1.4.0+8.0.1.jar` into `mods/`. **HalpLibe 6.1.4+8.0 is bundled inside it**,
so there is nothing else to install — if you already have a newer HalpLibe, yours still wins.

## You need your own copy of the original mod

This release ships none of the original's art. Download the original and drop it anywhere under your
game directory — any name, zipped or unpacked, client-side only:

https://b2.mcarchive.net/file/mcarchive/340befa2684a7336d8d5e7f418cc6e88c945f5596ab3edf73b4e157b527e09e7/ElementalCreepers_v1.4.zip

`ElementalCreepers_v1.4.zip` — 95 KB, sha256 `340befa2684a7336d8d5e7f418cc6e88c945f5596ab3edf73b4e157b527e09e7`

Without it everything still works; the eight skinned creepers just wear the vanilla creeper texture.

## Summoning

    /summon elementalcreepers:firecreeper

The namespace is required — BTA only accepts bare ids for its own mobs. The nine ids are printed at
startup under `Elemental Creepers summon ids:`.

## Playing with other mods

Registers no blocks, no items, no biomes, no dimensions and no world types, and uses no mixins, so
there is nothing to clash over. Its nine entities live under the `elementalcreepers:` namespace, and
BTA syncs entity ids from the server by namespaced string id, so load order cannot desynchronise a
client from a server.

Spawns are added by sweeping the biome registry after every mod has registered, so other mods'
biomes are covered automatically — including their Nether biomes, which the magma creeper needs. No
existing spawn entry is removed or reordered, and a biome whose monster list is already empty is
left completely alone.

Tested alongside Biomes O' Plenty and Twilight Forest.

## Requires

- Better than Adventure 8.0.1
- Java 17
